criteria.name: Trust-accounting and safekeeping analysis
criteria.description: Correctly identifies and analyzes the safekeeping-of-property duties at issue: commingling, failure to keep funds intact, delayed disbursement, absent accounting, and inadequate trust records. Draws the sanction-defining distinction between negligent commingling/recordkeeping and misappropriation.

subcriteria.name: Commingling vs. misappropriation
subcriteria.description: Distinguishes negligent commingling and recordkeeping violations from knowing use of client funds, and correctly locates the facts (including the borrowed funds) on that line.

subcriteria.name: Restitution and remediation framing
subcriteria.description: Accurately frames the absence of client loss, the voluntary interest, and the post-conduct remediation for their bearing on the violation and the sanction.

criteria.name: Diligence and communication analysis
criteria.description: Analyzes the failure-to-communicate count arising from the unreturned Osei calls, and its relationship to the diligence and communication duties, including the absence of a missed deadline or client loss.

criteria.name: Sanction analysis and proportionality
criteria.description: Marshals the aggravating and mitigating factors and builds a reasoned, proportionate argument for the recommended sanction consistent with the protective (not punitive) purpose of discipline.

subcriteria.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors
subcriteria.description: Identifies and weighs prior discipline, absence of dishonest motive, personal and health difficulties, restitution, cooperation, and remorse.

subcriteria.name: Proportionate sanction argument
subcriteria.description: Argues persuasively for the least severe appropriate sanction and confronts the misappropriation framing head-on.

criteria.name: Client interview and counseling
criteria.description: Conducts an interview that elicits the gated and concealed facts through rapport and confidentiality, handles the represented-witness contact question correctly, and counsels the distressed client candidly about disclosure versus concealment.

subcriteria.name: Fact elicitation and Rule 4.2 handling
subcriteria.description: Earns the rapport-gated and concealed facts and correctly routes contact with the represented complaining witness.

subcriteria.name: Counseling the distressed client
subcriteria.description: Counsels an ashamed, frightened lawyer-client about realistic outcomes and about candor duties without either judging or enabling concealment.

criteria.name: Respondent's pre-hearing brief
criteria.description: Produces a clear, well-organized, persuasive brief that concedes what must be conceded, argues the recommended sanction, and complies with form and length limits.

criteria.name: Oral argument and negotiation
criteria.description: Argues the sanction to the hearing panel, answers questions under pressure, and negotiates in good faith with disciplinary counsel toward a possible stipulated disposition.
